Subject: Re: Follow-up & a couple of clarifying q's after today's call

Hi Sofia / Kenji — thanks for the clear list. Nice to meet you both. Quick recap + deliverables we committed to below, and next steps.

Recap from today's discovery:
- Goal: Evaluate Redwood for customer-facing multilingual chat (product Q&A + returns flow) across EU and APAC locales.
- Key constraints: sub-200ms p50 token latency target for QA flows, support for EU data residency, and low hallucination on SKU/price-related prompts.

Deliverables (we'll send these by end of day 5/18):
1) Recommended model profiles: for initial smoke tests we suggest:
   - EU (DE/FR/NL): small-medium open model @ 16-bit + 4-bit quantized variant for cost testing ("redwood-base-1-16b" and "redwood-base-1-16b-q4") — good balance between generation quality and latency for 128–512 token windows.
   - APAC (JA/KO/ZH): slightly larger multilingual model with better CJK tokenization ("redwood-multi-2-13b") and a q4 variant for throughput testing.
2) Benchmark report: short PDF with p50/p95 latencies (128/512 windows) on a single A100-like SKU and on our Dedicated pool config (attached: benchmark_report_20270515.pdf).
3) Locale prompt sets: starter prompt set for DE/FR/JA + instructions for localized evaluation (attached: locale_prompt_set_v2.csv).
4) Quality checklist: prompt-level label guidelines, hallucination signals to monitor, and recommended unit tests (we'll paste key checks below).

Immediate ask of Globex: please confirm the list of critical languages (I have DE/FR/NL + JA/KO/ZH flagged) and whether you want us to include Portuguese/Spanish for EU. Also confirm if you have a preferred time for a technical deep-dive next week (we can loop in our inference engineer).

Quick notes on quality regressions: we will include a small eval harness with reference prompts and expected outputs; if you see regression vs your baseline, we recommend: 1) try the q4 variant on a handful of prompts; 2) lock model weights and run an A/B on a canary fraction; 3) instrument token-level attribution to spot prompt patterns that trigger hallucination.

Attachments: locale_prompt_set_v2.csv (starter prompts), benchmark_report_20270515.pdf (internal run against redwood-multi-2-13b/q4).

Next steps:
- Marissa / Rishi: schedule technical deep-dive call (30–45m) for next week.
- Globex: confirm languages to prioritize and add any additional prompt examples (Kenji for JA).
- Target: procurement-ready vendor summary by 2027-06-02.

Thanks — will follow up with the artifacts as promised.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Kenji / Sofia — thanks, and great questions. Short answers + action items below.

1) Tokenization for Japanese:
   - redwood-multi-2-13b uses a SentencePiece-based tokenizer with a vocabulary tuned for CJK languages to preserve common morphological units. In our tests we've found better verb/particle boundaries vs naive byte-level tokenizers. That said, please avoid over-tokenized punctuation in prompts (no repeated punctuation runs) and prefer natural spacing in Japanese.
   - Action: attached is a short "tokenization_tips.txt" excerpt in the prompt CSV comments and the locale_prompt_set_v2.csv includes canonicalized JA examples.

2) Latency numbers (JA-specific):
   - p50 (128 tokens) on single A100-like SKU: 120ms
   - p95 (128 tokens): 280ms
   - p50 (512 tokens): 260ms
   - Dedicated pool (reserved RDUs x4): p50 (128 tokens): 90ms
   These are callout numbers; full breakdown is in the attached PDF under the "Per-locale breakdown" section (see page 3).

3) Prompt labeling schema:
   - Yes, please follow the same label schema in the CSV (intent, expected_answer, hallucination_flag, critical_entity). We'll add a sample QA pair for JA and a short rubric for scoring (0–3).
   - Action: Kenji to upload the additional 50 JA prompts to the shared Drive folder; Marissa/Rishi will run a small automated pass and return a short quality report within 48 hours.

4) Technical sync:
   - Rishi (cc'd) can join Wed 5/19 09:00 JST / Tue 5/18 17:00 PDT for a 20-minute sync. Rishi, Vivek — can you confirm?

Attachments in this reply: locale_prompt_set_v2.csv (with JA examples), benchmark_report_20270515.pdf (per-locale appendix).

- Rishi: run the quick quality pass and return a one-page summary (due 5/20).
- Marissa: prepare the procurement-ready vendor summary (due 6/2).

Let me know if you'd prefer we scope a more formal POC with a 2-week canary on Dedicated capacity (we can provide pricing scenarios).

Best,
